items.question: Which recommended airspeed should be used for takeoff and climb in the R44 II?
items.explanation: The RECOMMENDED AIRSPEEDS table lists 60 KIAS as the recommended airspeed for takeoff and climb.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: RECOMMENDED AIRSPEEDS (p.4-1)

items.question: What is the recommended airspeed for maximum rate of climb (VY) in the R44 II?
items.explanation: The table specifies Maximum Rate of Climb (VY) as 55 KIAS.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: RECOMMENDED AIRSPEEDS (p.4-1)

items.question: Which recommended airspeed should be used for landing approach in the R44 II?
items.explanation: The RECOMMENDED AIRSPEEDS table lists Landing Approach at 60 KIAS.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: RECOMMENDED AIRSPEEDS (p.4-1)

items.question: In significant turbulence, which indicated airspeed range is recommended?
items.explanation: For significant turbulence the table recommends 60 to 70 KIAS.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: RECOMMENDED AIRSPEEDS (p.4-1)

items.question: What is the recommended airspeed range for autorotation in the R44 II, according to the Normal Procedures section?
items.explanation: The RECOMMENDED AIRSPEEDS table lists Autorotation at 60 to 70 KIAS (with note that some conditions may require lower airspeed).
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: RECOMMENDED AIRSPEEDS (p.4-1)

items.question: Before flight, how should frost, ice or snow on the rotor blades be handled during the daily or preflight checks?
items.explanation: The DAILY OR PREFLIGHT CHECKS state that even small accumulations of frost, ice or snow, especially from rotor blades, must be removed.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: DAILY OR PREFLIGHT CHECKS (p.4-1)

items.question: What piece of equipment is recommended to assist with preflight inspection of the main rotor on the R44 II?
items.explanation: The text notes that an 8-foot step ladder is recommended for preflight inspection of the main rotor.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: DAILY OR PREFLIGHT CHECKS (p.4-1)

items.question: When inspecting the helicopter during daily or preflight checks, what does black powder at rivets and seams typically indicate?
items.explanation: The POH explains that fretting of aluminum parts produces a fine black powder, while fretting of steel parts produces a reddish-brown or black residue.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: DAILY OR PREFLIGHT CHECKS (p.4-1)

items.question: According to the daily or preflight checks, what should be verified on Telatemp indicators?
options: That they have turned completely white
That they show no temperature increase not explained by operating conditions
That they all read the same temperature
That they match outside air temperature
items.explanation: The checklist says to verify Telatemps show no temperature increase that cannot be attributed to a change in operating conditions.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: DAILY OR PREFLIGHT CHECKS (p.4-1)

items.question: What is the purpose of torque stripes on critical fasteners during the daily or preflight check?
options: They show if a fastener has moved or loosened
items.explanation: The text directs the pilot to verify torque stripes on critical fasteners are not broken or missing, indicating no movement.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: DAILY OR PREFLIGHT CHECKS (p.4-1)

items.question: Before starting the engine, what is the required position of the fuel shut-off valve?
items.explanation: In the BEFORE STARTING ENGINE checklist, the fuel shut-off valve is listed as ON.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: BEFORE STARTING ENGINE (p.4-6)

items.question: How should the cyclic, collective and pedals be checked before engine start according to the checklist?
options: Cyclic neutral only; other controls not moved
Full travel free for cyclic, collective and pedals
items.explanation: The BEFORE STARTING ENGINE items specify cyclic, collective and pedals with full travel free.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: BEFORE STARTING ENGINE (p.4-6)

items.question: In the before-start checklist, how is the collective set when friction is applied?
items.explanation: The checklist states: Collective – full down, friction ON before engine start.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: BEFORE STARTING ENGINE (p.4-6)

items.question: During engine starting, when should the mixture be moved to full rich in the normal start sequence?
options: After the starter is engaged and the engine fires
After the clutch light goes out
items.explanation: The STARTING ENGINE AND RUN-UP procedure describes pulling mixture OFF, engaging the starter, and then moving mixture full rich as the engine fires.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: STARTING ENGINE AND RUN-UP (p.4-7)

items.question: According to Engine Starting Tips, when priming for a normal start, how long should the fuel pump be run after the caution light extinguishes?
items.explanation: ENGINE STARTING TIPS instructs the pilot to prime 3 to 5 seconds after the fuel pump caution light extinguishes.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: ENGINE STARTING TIPS (p.4-7)

items.question: During the upper forward cowl door check on the right side, what should be done with the fuel tank sump and gascolator drains?
options: Leave them closed and visually inspect only
Open them fully during each preflight
Use them only if contamination is suspected
items.explanation: The DAILY OR PREFLIGHT CHECKS specify that the fuel tank sump and gascolator drains should be sampled.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: DAILY OR PREFLIGHT CHECKS (p.4-2)

items.question: When checking the main rotor during the daily or preflight inspection, how should a blade be lowered?
options: Pull down directly on the blade you want to lower
Push up on the opposite blade
Push down on the hub with both hands
Use a rope tied to the blade tip
items.explanation: The POH cautions not to pull down on blades to teeter the rotor; to lower a blade, push up on the opposite blade.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: DAILY OR PREFLIGHT CHECKS (p.4-2)

items.question: During preflight with the left cowl door open, what engine oil quantity is specified?
items.explanation: The DAILY OR PREFLIGHT CHECKS list engine oil quantity as 7-9 quarts.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: DAILY OR PREFLIGHT CHECKS (p.4-4)

items.question: What caution is given regarding loading baggage compartments under the seats?
options: Fill compartments under occupied seats before unoccupied seats
Fill compartments under unoccupied seats before compartments under occupied seats
Do not use baggage compartments under seats
items.explanation: The POH cautions to fill baggage compartments under unoccupied seats to capacity before using compartments under occupied seats to reduce risk of injury if a seat collapses in a hard landing.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: DAILY OR PREFLIGHT CHECKS (p.4-6)

items.question: Before starting the engine, what is the required position of the rotor brake?
items.explanation: The BEFORE STARTING ENGINE checklist specifies the rotor brake as disengaged.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: BEFORE STARTING ENGINE (p.4-6)

items.question: According to the before-start checklist, how should the HYD and governor switches be set?
items.explanation: The BEFORE STARTING ENGINE checklist calls for HYD and governor switches ON.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: BEFORE STARTING ENGINE (p.4-6)

items.question: During engine start and run-up, what is the minimum oil pressure that must be seen within 30 seconds?
items.explanation: The STARTING ENGINE AND RUN-UP checklist specifies oil pressure within 30 seconds at a minimum of 25 psi.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: STARTING ENGINE AND RUN-UP (p.4-7)

items.question: At 75% RPM during the run-up, what is the maximum allowable magneto drop and time limit?
items.explanation: The POH states that at 75% RPM mag drop should be 7% maximum in 2 seconds.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: STARTING ENGINE AND RUN-UP (p.4-7)

items.question: During warm-up, what rotor RPM range is recommended before increasing to full operating RPM?
items.explanation: The checklist calls for warm-up at 60 to 70% RPM.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: STARTING ENGINE AND RUN-UP (p.4-7)

items.question: With the governor ON prior to takeoff, what rotor RPM range should be set for normal flight?
items.explanation: The STARTING ENGINE AND RUN-UP procedure ends with governor ON and throttle increased to achieve 101-102% RPM.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: STARTING ENGINE AND RUN-UP (p.4-7)

items.question: In the takeoff procedure, what should be done immediately after raising the helicopter into a hover?
options: Check that all warning lights are illuminated
Check gages in the green and note hover MAP
Turn HYD and governor switches OFF
items.explanation: During TAKEOFF PROCEDURE, after establishing a hover the pilot should check gages in the green and note hover manifold pressure.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: TAKEOFF PROCEDURE (p.4-9)

items.question: According to the takeoff procedure, what is the recommended limit on manifold pressure above IGE hover power to avoid excessive nose-down attitude?
items.explanation: The POH cautions to avoid exceeding two inches MAP above IGE hover power.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: TAKEOFF PROCEDURE (p.4-9)

items.question: During takeoff, if rotor RPM drops below 101%, what immediate action is recommended?
items.explanation: The TAKEOFF PROCEDURE section states that if RPM drops below 101%, the pilot should lower collective.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: TAKEOFF PROCEDURE (p.4-9)

items.question: With any door or combination of doors removed, what is the maximum approved airspeed for the R44 II?
items.explanation: The DOORS-OFF OPERATION section limits airspeed to 100 KIAS with any door(s) off.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: DOORS-OFF OPERATION (p.4-9)

items.question: Why is flight with left door or doors removed not recommended in the R44 II?
options: Loose objects exiting left doors may damage the tail rotor
It causes uncorrectable yaw to the right
items.explanation: The DOORS-OFF OPERATION section states that flight with left door(s) removed is not recommended because loose objects exiting the left doors may damage the tail rotor.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: DOORS-OFF OPERATION (p.4-9)

items.question: During cruise, how must the engine mixture control be used according to the Normal Procedures section?
options: It may be leaned in smooth air
It may be leaned only above 5000 ft
It must remain full rich in flight
It may be set anywhere as long as CHT is in green
items.explanation: The CRUISE section states that in-flight leaning with the engine mixture control is not allowed and that the mixture must be full rich during flight.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: CRUISE (p.4-10)

items.question: When the helicopter is loaded near the aft CG limit in cruise, what technique is recommended to stop slight yaw oscillation?
options: Apply a small amount of left pedal
Apply a small amount of right pedal
items.explanation: The CRUISE section notes that slight yaw oscillation near the aft CG limit can be stopped by applying a small amount of left pedal.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: CRUISE (p.4-10)

items.question: For noise abatement, what minimum altitude above outdoor assemblies of people is recommended when overflight cannot be avoided?
items.explanation: The NOISE ABATEMENT section recommends flying as high as practical, preferably over 2000 feet AGL, when overflying outdoor assemblies of people.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: NOISE ABATEMENT (p.4-15)

items.question: To avoid blade slap during approaches, what technique is described in the noise abatement section?
options: Maintain 100 KIAS until rate of descent exceeds 1000 fpm, then use a fairly steep approach until airspeed is below about 65 KIAS
Always approach at 60 KIAS and less than 300 fpm
Keep collective high and airspeed low throughout the approach
items.explanation: The NOISE ABATEMENT section explains that blade slap can usually be avoided by maintaining 100 KIAS until rate of descent is over 1000 fpm, then using a fairly steep approach until airspeed is below about 65 KIAS.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: NOISE ABATEMENT (p.4-15)

items.question: According to the noise abatement guidance, what general altitude policy should be followed when flying over populated or noise-sensitive areas?
options: Fly above 500 ft AGL and preferably above 1000 ft AGL
Always climb to at least 3000 ft AGL
Stay at pattern altitude regardless of area
items.explanation: The NOISE ABATEMENT section recommends flying above 500 ft AGL and preferably above 1000 ft AGL and avoiding prolonged flight over noise-sensitive areas.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: NOISE ABATEMENT (p.4-15)

items.question: When practicing autorotation with power recovery, how should throttle be reduced to simulate power failure?
options: Leave throttle fixed and lower collective only
Turn the governor OFF first, then chop throttle
items.explanation: The PRACTICE AUTOROTATION – POWER RECOVERY section cautions not to chop throttle to simulate power failure and to always roll throttle off smoothly.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: PRACTICE AUTOROTATION – POWER RECOVERY (p.4-11)

items.question: At approximately what engine RPM does the governor become inactive regardless of switch position?
items.explanation: A note in the PRACTICE AUTOROTATION – POWER RECOVERY section states that the governor is inactive below 80% engine RPM regardless of switch position.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: PRACTICE AUTOROTATION – POWER RECOVERY (p.4-11)

items.question: When entering autorotation from above 6000 feet, what additional step is recommended to prevent engine overspeed?
options: Lower collective rapidly before reducing throttle
Reduce throttle slightly before lowering collective
Turn the governor OFF before entry
items.explanation: The POH notes that when entering autorotation from above 6000 feet, throttle should be reduced slightly before lowering collective to prevent engine overspeed.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: PRACTICE AUTOROTATION – POWER RECOVERY (p.4-11)

items.question: What rotor RPM caution is given for simulated engine failures to avoid catastrophic rotor stall?
options: Never allow rotor RPM below 85% plus 1% per 1000 ft
Never allow rotor RPM below 80% plus 1% per 1000 ft
Never allow rotor RPM below 75% plus 2% per 1000 ft
items.explanation: The caution states that catastrophic rotor stall could occur if rotor RPM ever drops below 80% plus 1% per 1000 feet of altitude.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: PRACTICE AUTOROTATION – POWER RECOVERY (p.4-11)

items.question: When simulating hydraulic failure using the cyclic-mounted hydraulic switch, what caution is given about hovering with hydraulics switched OFF?
options: Hovering will require significantly more collective
Controlling the helicopter in a hover may be difficult due to control system feedback forces
Hovering may cause immediate hydraulic system damage
items.explanation: The HYDRAULICS-OFF TRAINING section cautions that with hydraulics switched OFF, controlling the helicopter in a hover may be difficult due to feedback forces.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: HYDRAULICS-OFF TRAINING (p.4-12)

items.question: Before switching the hydraulic system from OFF back to ON, what should the pilot do with cyclic and collective forces?
options: Hold firm pressure to maintain attitude
Apply aft cyclic and lower collective
Relax force on cyclic and collective
Move controls rapidly through full travel
items.explanation: The HYDRAULICS-OFF TRAINING section cautions that before switching hydraulics from OFF to ON, the pilot should relax force on cyclic and collective to avoid over-controlling.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: HYDRAULICS-OFF TRAINING (p.4-12)

items.question: When initiating a descent, why must the pilot avoid using forward cyclic to start the descent?
options: It may reduce tail rotor effectiveness
It can produce a low-G condition
It increases engine manifold pressure too quickly
It may cause retreating blade stall
items.explanation: The DESCENT, APPROACH, AND LANDING section cautions not to initiate a descent with forward cyclic because this can produce a low-G condition; descents should be initiated by lowering collective.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: DESCENT, APPROACH, AND LANDING (p.4-13)

items.question: During final approach and landing, what rate-of-descent condition should be met before reducing airspeed below 30 KIAS?
options: Rate of descent less than 100 fpm
Rate of descent less than 200 fpm
Rate of descent less than 300 fpm
Rate of descent less than 400 fpm
items.explanation: The DESCENT, APPROACH, AND LANDING section specifies that the rate of descent should be less than 300 FPM before airspeed is reduced below 30 KIAS.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: DESCENT, APPROACH, AND LANDING (p.4-13)

items.question: During shutdown, why must the pilot not slow the rotor by raising collective?
options: It may cause rapid clutch wear
It may cause blades to flap and strike the tailcone
It will overheat the rotor brake
items.explanation: The SHUTDOWN PROCEDURE cautions not to slow the rotor by raising collective because blades may flap and strike the tailcone.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: SHUTDOWN PROCEDURE (p.4-14)

items.question: After shutdown, why is the rotor brake recommended to be left engaged?
options: To keep the rotor blades aligned with the fuselage
To prevent the transmission from cooling too quickly
To disable starter buttons and reduce the possibility of unintentional starter engagement
To ensure the hydraulic system remains pressurized
items.explanation: The SHUTDOWN PROCEDURE notes that the rotor brake should be left engaged after shutdown to disable starter buttons and reduce the possibility of unintentional starter engagement.
references: R44 II POH Sec 4: SHUTDOWN PROCEDURE (p.4-14)
